items.rationale: Column i is the endpoint's twist (linear and angular velocity) produced by joint i alone at unit rate. Option a treats the Jacobian as derivatives of Euler angles; b sums all joints into one vector; d measures frame i's origin instead of the endpoint.
The moment arm runs from joint 1 to the endpoint: 0.4 + 0.3 = 0.7 m, so v = 2 x 0.7 = 1.4 m/s. An answer of 0.8 uses only link 1's length (M4).

The angular part of a rotary column is the joint axis in base coordinates. Rotating +y by 90 degrees counterclockwise about +z gives -x, so the x-component is -1. An answer of 0 uses the local-frame axis (0,0,1) or ignores the turn of joint 1 (M7); +1 flips the rotation direction.

A sliding joint moves the endpoint along its axis at the joint rate and cannot rotate it, so linear part z and angular part 0. Options b and d apply the rotary cross product to a prismatic joint; c gives it an angular part.

A rotary joint turns everything beyond it about its axis at the joint rate, so the angular part of its column is the axis (0,0,1) in base coordinates, independent of link lengths. Link lengths only enter the linear part.

Moving the reference point changes the moment arm, so the cross-product linear part of each rotary column changes. Angular parts belong to the whole rigid body and stay the same, and a prismatic column's linear part is just its axis, so it does not change either.
